How long has this pruritic rash and fever been present, and have you noticed any specific rash patterns like the "slapped cheek" appearance or a lacy rash on your extremities?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC Normal; Hemoglobin Normal; Platelets Slightly elevated. Dermatology_Skin_Rash: Lacy, reticular rash noted on the trunk and extremities. Facial rash present but sparing the perioral area. Rash is slightly raised but not accompanied by significant warmth or tenderness.

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Attends local school. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No recent travel history.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any respiratory distress, joint pains, or changes in bowel or urinary habits. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is surprising; Pyelonephritis typically presents with flank pain and fever, but not with a pruritic rash or the respiratory symptoms you described earlier. Can you describe the exact appearance of your rash and confirm if you have had any joint pain since our initial conversation?

REQUEST TEST: Anti-Erythema Infectiosum IgM (Parvovirus B19)
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_Skin_Rash

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Anti-Erythema Infectiosum IgM (Parvovirus B19): Positive. Dermatology_Skin_Rash: Lacy, reticular rash noted on the trunk and extremities. Facial rash present but sparing the perioral area. Rash is slightly raised but not accompanied by significant warmth or tenderness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19 infection.
